The European Parliament’s Foreign Affairs Committee Chair, David McAllister, has said that the India-EU Free Trade Agreement (FTA) is expected to be signed by mid-December 2026, with PM Narendra Modi anticipated to travel to Brussels for the official signing ceremony.The "mother of all deals" will still undergo rigorous scrutiny by the European Parliament, but McAllister told TOI in an interview he's confident about smooth ratification, given the benefits it will bring to both sides. The EU lawmaker said that a consent vote is expected by spring next year, paving the way for the trade agreement to officially enter into force mid-2027."We expect the FTA to be signed by mid-December. Hopefully, PM Modi will manage to visit Brussels and attend the official signing ceremony," said McAllister, who led an EU Parliamentary delegation to India this week."Though Parliament cannot amend the text of the agreement, our consent is required before it enters into force. I followed the debate in the European Parliament over the past months, and I can say there seems to be a broad majority support for this landmark FTA. The benefits for both sides are so huge that I'm sure the European Parliament will give its support in the consent vote," added McAllister, who heads the Parliamentary committee that shapes and monitors the EU's common foreign and security policy.McAllister also said the EU would particularly welcome progress on the investment protection agreement as it would strengthen the confidence of European investors in the Indian market, encouraging greater European investments and contributing to job creation in India. He said the FTA would allow India and the EU to work more closely on de-risking supply chains and reducing dependencies.If the FTA indeed is ready for signing by mid-December, Modi is likely to stop over in Brussels to ink the deal on his way back to India from the US G20 summit. The PM will also travel to Canada and possibly to Germany during that trip.Asked about the prospects of defence-industrial collaboration and technology sharing under the new India-EU defence and security partnership, McAllister backed closer cooperation between India and the European defence industry, saying it is in the interest of both sides. He also spoke about the convergence of interest in keeping the Indo-Pacific free and open and the need to reduce reliance on any one country"There are many fields of cooperation in this matter. I would definitely mention information sharing, research cooperation and cybersecurity. One element would be that we also invite India to participate in a closer cooperation with our European defense industry, because here we also have a joint interest," said the lawmaker."We in Europe, as part of our strategic sovereignty, want to reduce the dependence on one particular country, and I understand that the debate in India is very similar. You also want to step-by-step reduce your dependence, and I think this is a very good win-win situation for both sides," said McAllister.Asked about India's position on the Russia-Ukraine war, McAllister welcomed the Modi government's diplomatic efforts to achieve a ceasefire covering energy infrastructure, Black Sea shipping, and the movement of grain."Any peace agreement must be just, sustainable and acceptable to both sides. It must also include absolute, concrete security guarantees for Ukraine that Putin (Russian president) is not able to repeat this unbelievable act of aggression and violation of international law. So, if India with its special relationship with Russia - and also India with its constructive relationship with Ukraine - can play any kind of role constructively, it would be welcome," he said, while praising Jaishankar's "constructive" role for peace.
Article Summary: European Parliament’s Foreign Affairs Committee Chair, David McAllister, has said that the India-EU Free Trade Agreement is expected to be signed by mid- December 2026. PM Narendra Modi is anticipated to travel to Brussels for the official signing ceremony. The EU lawmaker said that a consent vote is expected by spring next year.

Article Title: Half of Gen Z’s beauty buyers on Myntra come from smaller cities: Report
Article Text:
Beauty in the Age of Gen Z

Speaking on the launch of the report, Sharon Pais, Head of Myntra, said,

Minis and creators:

Beyond the metros:

Prevention, ingredients and K-Beauty:

Repeat shoppers:

Backing Indian brands:

Disclaimer: This article has been produced on behalf of Myntra by Times Internet’s Spotlight team.

For Gen Z, beauty is becoming less about covering up imperfections and more about building everyday routines around skincare, personal expression and informed product choices. From prioritising prevention over correction to checking ingredient lists before making a purchase, young consumers are changing what they expect from beauty products and the brands that sell them.Their influence is also extending beyond India’s metropolitan markets. Smaller product formats let consumers try premium beauty products at a lower cost before committing to full-sized purchases, while the growing emphasis on skincare reflects a shift toward regular care rather than occasional fixes. Together, these behaviour point to a generation that is approaching beauty with greater awareness of ingredients, affordability and individual needs.These shifts are among the findings of, a new report released by Myntra. The report examines how younger consumers are reshaping India’s beauty market, with ingredient-led choices, preventive skincare and wider access to premium products emerging as key themes.Gen Z and millennials are both growing the beauty and personal care category on Myntra, with Gen Z giving the category a 75% higher share of its wallet. Self-expression comes first for this generation, and the category is one of the clearest places it shows. Gen Z’s beauty and personal care spend per customer is up 1.2X YoY alongside a fast growing customer base on Myntra. Half of Gen Z’s beauty buyers on Myntra live in Tier 2 and 3 cities. Sun protection (SPF) products are up 60% YoY among Gen Z shoppers, and 53% of luxe makeup orders on Myntra now include a mini.Gen Z is shaping a market that industry reports* expect to grow from ~$23bn to ~$40bn. India still spends only ~$15 per head on beauty, against $38 in China and $383 in the US, according to the industry reports*.“Beauty and personal care is one of Myntra’s strongest growth engines. For Gen Z, beauty is self-expression. It’s how they show up, plan their looks and live their social lives. They try premium and international brands through minis, find new ones through creators and K-Beauty, and choose on ingredients and efficacy, in cities across the country. The brands that win will meet this shopper early, make discovery easy and earn trust through the product and its ingredients. ”As per the report, Minis make up 14% of luxe units sold, led by lipstick, perfume and face primer. Brands such as M.A.C, Kayali, Smashbox and Salvatore Ferragamo get more than half of their new customers through minis. Video is how Gen Z finds beauty. Myntra has ~82,000 active beauty creators, UGC beauty content is up 40% YoY, and nearly 2 in 3 new beauty creator registrations over the last four months are Gen Z.Gen Z baskets in Tier 2 and 3 cities include serums, toners, sunscreens and hair masks alongside everyday staples. These cities account for half of the platform's international beauty demand. Ludhiana, Patna, Bhopal, Indore, Guwahati, Surat, Varanasi and Imphal are among the cities driving growth, according to the report.Sun protection has become a year-round habit among Gen Z shoppers, with searches up 80% for spray sunscreens, 70% for ingredient-led sunscreens and 60% for tinted sunscreens (SPF, or sun protection factor). Gel-based, fragrance-free and non-sticky textures are in demand, and Gen Z is seeking out ingredients such as Centella asiatica, copper peptides, azelaic acid and panthenol.K-Beauty demand grew 200% YoY and searches rose more than 300%. Myntra now offers 1,000+ SKUs from 90+ K-Beauty brands, with 30+ added in the last year. Hair masks grew 110%, against 59% for conditioners, and men's skincare orders grew 78% YoY, led by Gen Z.Repeat Gen Z orders on Myntra are up ~70% this year, and the repeat beauty shopper and the repeat apparel shopper are more often than not the same person.Beauty is roughly 1 in 5 units ordered on Myntra, is growing at twice the online beauty market, and brought in nearly half a million new customers in May 2026 alone. Myntra offers ~2.5 lakh styles from 4,500+ brands, including 360+ international brands. Virtual Try-On makes shoppers 2X more likely to buy, and Skin Analyzer lifts conversion by ~58%. Beauty on M-Now spans ~600 brands, with delivery as quick as nine minutes.Myntra hosts 700 pure-play D2C beauty brands and 3,000 emerging D2C names, and D2C beauty has grown 68% so far in FY26. Plum, Minimalist, Foxtale, The Derma Co. and Chemist at Play are among those driving growth. Gen Z is 25% likelier to try an indigenous or D2C brand. Gen Z and millennial shoppers are both backing these brands, with Gen Z among the quickest to try them.Gen Z's wishlist already points to what's next, including lactic acid, tranexamic acid and foundation-SPF hybrids. Myntra's focus moves to scale and share, with a better pre- and post-purchase experience, a stronger ecosystem through Myntra GlamStream, and continued momentum in D2C, luxury, international beauty, non-metros and first-time online beauty shoppers.The report was unveiled at the Myntra Beauty IRL event in Mumbai, alongside a panel discussion on The New Indian Beauty Consumer.The report is based on Myntra platform data, buying behaviour and search trends from August 2025 to August 2026, covering Gen Z shoppers, and is read alongside trend-spotting by Myntra's creative and curation teams.*Market estimates are from Redseer.
Article Summary: New report examines how younger consumers are reshaping India’s beauty market. Smaller product formats let consumers try premium beauty products at a lower cost before committing to full-sized purchases. Sun protection products are up 60% YoY among Gen Z shoppers, and 53% of luxe makeup orders on Myntra now include a mini.

Article Title: SC disposes of Mahua Moitra's plea seeking public disclosure of AIF, FPI beneficiaries
Article Text:
TMC MP Mahua Moitra approached the Supreme Court seeking public disclosure of the ultimate beneficial owners of AIFs and FPIs, but the Court dismissed her plea, citing the absence of a legal framework mandating such disclosure.

Join conversation View All Comments → Share your thoughts in the comments Insightful Agree Disagree Skeptical Concerning Promising Worth Reading Big Development Post Comment Be respectful · TOI community guidelines

NEW DELHI: The Supreme Court on Thursday disposed of Trinamool Congress MP Mahua Moitra's plea seeking public disclosure of the ultimate beneficial owners and portfolio holdings of alternative investment funds (AIFs), foreign portfolio investors (FPIs) and their intermediaries, saying it could not issue directions in the absence of a legal framework mandating such disclosures.A bench of Justices BV Nagarathna, R Mahadevan and DK Upadhyaya said there was no existing legal regime requiring full public disclosure of the ultimate beneficial owners of these funds. It said the court could direct the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) to ensure compliance if such a framework existed, but could not issue a mandamus without one."Had there been any legal regime and the SEBI was not following it, the court can direct for compliance but in the absence of any framework or legal regime, the court cannot issue any mandamus," it observed.The bench also questioned Moitra's decision to approach the court, suggesting that she could have raised the issue in Parliament and sought a discussion on it.Advocate Prashant Bhushan, appearing for Moitra, argued that the court could direct SEBI to ensure full disclosure of the actual beneficiaries of these funds even in the absence of a specific regulatory framework. He contended that innocent investors were being "manipulated" by investors who artificially boosted the share prices of companies.In her public interest litigation (PIL), Moitra sought greater transparency and investor awareness in India's financial markets by making details of the ultimate beneficial owners and portfolio holdings of AIFs and FPIs publicly available.The plea noted that SEBI regulates India's securities markets and oversees the operations of AIFs and FPIs as part of its mandate.
Article Summary: TMC MP Mahua Moitra approached the Supreme Court seeking public disclosure of the ultimate beneficial owners of AIFs and FPIs. The Court dismissed her plea, citing the absence of a legal framework mandating such disclosure. It said the court could direct the Securities and Exchange Board of India (SEBI) to ensure compliance if such a framework existed.

NEW DELHI: Union Culture Minister Gajendra Singh Shekhawat on Wednesday said India is not merely an entity confined within geographical boundaries but a cultural nation shaped by thousands of years of continuity, knowledge, struggle and experience.Shekhawat was addressing a gathering at the launch of the book 'Timeless India: Protection & Revival of Indian Cultural Identity under the Leadership of Prime Minister Narendra Modi' at the Dharohar Bhawan, the headquarters of the Archaeological Survey of India (ASI), which hosted the event along with the Indira Gandhi National Centre for the Arts (IGNCA).The book has been published by IGNCA and Subhi Publications and edited by former Rajya Sabha member Tarun Vijay."India is not merely an entity confined within geographical boundaries, but a cultural nation shaped by thousands of years of continuity, knowledge, spiritual practice, struggle and experience. Article Title: Watch: Tamil Nadu CM Vijay launches one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns
Article Text:
Vijay presented 22-carat, one-gram gold rings to 25 newborns. (PTI)

Who is eligible for the gold ring?

Scheme draws on Tamil tradition

NEW DELHI: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Monday rolled out the state government’s one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns in Madurai. He also held some of the newborns and presented the rings to beneficiaries during the launch programme.Under the scheme, eligible babies born in government hospitals and government primary health centres will receive a 22-carat, one-gram gold ring.The initiative, named the Maternal Uncle Gold Ring Scheme (Thaaimaman Thanga Mothiram Thittam), has an annual allocation of Rs 755.83 crore.It is aimed at celebrating motherhood, promoting maternal and child health and encouraging institutional deliveries by increasing public confidence in government healthcare facilities.The scheme will cover babies born on or after June 22, 2026, to mothers who are permanent residents of Tamil Nadu and have delivered at government healthcare institutions.Mothers must be registered under the Pregnancy and Infant Cohort Monitoring and Evaluation (PICME) system and have a Reproductive and Child Health (RCH) ID. They will also have to provide an e-KYC-verified Aadhaar card along with one of the prescribed identity or residence documents.These include ration cards, voter identity cards, Labour Welfare Board identity cards, Department of Posts address cards and nativity certificates.The state government has already procured 1.28 lakh one-gram gold rings for the initial rollout. Each ring will have a unique serial number and will be packed in tamper-proof packaging.From Monday, babies born in government hospitals will receive the rings at the time of discharge, according to the state government.To clear the backlog of eligible babies born between June 22 and Monday, the government will distribute the rings through 107 hubs across Tamil Nadu.Distribution will begin at the rate of 100 babies per day at each hub. At designated centres, 25 beneficiaries will be accommodated in the morning and another 25 in the afternoon to avoid overcrowding, PTI reported.Village Health Nurses will distribute invitations informing beneficiaries of their allotted date and time. Beneficiaries have been asked to visit the designated centres only at the time mentioned in their invitations.The district administration has also made transportation arrangements for beneficiaries from their respective areas. Vijay had announced the scheme ahead of the April 23 Assembly election as a symbolic gift to newborns, drawing on the Tamil tradition of ‘Thaimaaman Seer’. The scheme has retrospective effect from June 22, Vijay’s birthday.A government order issued on June 23 described the initiative as a token celebrating the birth of a child, motherhood and the cultural tradition of ‘Thaimaaman’.According to ANI, Tamil Nadu minister Arun Raj explained the cultural significance of the initiative saying, "A maternal uncle is someone who is among the first to rush in when a child is born, sharing in his sister’s happiness as his own. He assures her that he will always stand by her and her child, offering love, support and a sense of security.""Today, the Tamil Nadu Government, under the leadership of our brother, Mr. Vijay, is embracing this sacred bond of the maternal uncle and, as a gesture of that affection, is set to provide a one-gram gold ring to every child born in government hospitals. When the scheme was announced and the question arose as to where it should be launched, the place chosen by our Chief Minister was Madurai. This is the sacred soil of Madurai, blessed with the compassion and grace of Mother Meenakshi," he added.Tamil Nadu records around 7.8 lakh deliveries annually, with institutional deliveries accounting for 99.9% of births, according to NFHS-6. Government health facilities account for nearly 4.2 lakh deliveries, or around 53% of the total.According to the state government, the average out-of-pocket expenditure for a delivery at a government hospital is Rs 1,364, compared with Rs 63,473 at a private hospital.The government said the scheme is intended to encourage safe institutional deliveries, strengthen maternal and child welfare and increase public trust in government healthcare services.The Tamil Nadu Medical Services Corporation will procure the gold rings based on annual requirements, while a project and programme management unit will oversee implementation and monitoring.
Article Summary: Tamil Nadu chief minister C Joseph Vijay on Monday rolled out the state government’s one-gram gold ring scheme for newborns in Madurai. The scheme will cover babies born on or after June 22, 2026, to mothers who are permanent residents of Tamil Nadu and have delivered at government healthcare institutions. Vijay had announced the scheme ahead of the April 23 Assembly election.

NEW DELHI: Delhi chief minister Rekha Gupta on Saturday said the garbage mountains at the city's landfill sites were steadily shrinking as she reviewed waste disposal work at Okhla and laid the foundation stone for new waste processing facilities at Okhla, Ghazipur and Singhola.Gupta said the Delhi government had reclaimed 100 acres of land across the city's three landfill sites over the past one-and-a-half years, with a large portion of the cleared area also being turned green.She said almost all legacy waste at Okhla that existed before January 2025 had been processed."Today, at Okhla, we have processed almost all the legacy waste that was there before January 2025," Gupta said.Gupta said the government was working on two fronts: clearing the existing garbage mountains while ensuring that fresh waste generated every day did not accumulate into new landfill sites.According to news agency ANI, she said around 3,000-4,000 metric tonnes of fresh waste reaches the sites daily and is being processed round the clock."The garbage currently piled up here is essentially fresh waste generated after January 2025, and that too is being processed round the clock. So, we are fighting on two fronts: one is eliminating waste, and the other is ensuring that the 3,000 to 4,000 metric tons of fresh waste arriving daily is processed immediately, so that new garbage mountains are not formed for future generations," Gupta said.She said the government was working to reduce the existing garbage mountains to zero."People are seeing that the garbage mountains are continuously shrinking and soon a time will come when they will become zero," Gupta said.Gupta also said she had taken what she described as her "last selfie" with the garbage mountain at Okhla."Today I have taken my last selfie with the garbage mountain; after this I have taken a pledge that this garbage mountain will end soon," she said.Taking a jibe at the Opposition, Gupta added, "I had said - garbage mountain, you will have to go; the opposition mocked. Today I will say the garbage mountain is going; now only its back remains."During the programme at the Okhla SLF site, Gupta laid the foundation stone for fresh waste processing plants at Okhla, Ghazipur and Singhola, as well as a biogas facility at Ghazipur. She also inaugurated the M&CW Centre at Kotla Mubarakpur through virtual mode from Okhla.The Okhla plant will be built at a cost of Rs 103 crore and will have a processing capacity of 1,400 metric tonnes per day.The Singhola facility will cost Rs 42 crore and have a capacity of 800 metric tonnes per day, while the Ghazipur plant will have a processing capacity of 700 metric tonnes per day.The facilities are intended to process fresh waste as well as construction and demolition waste. Gupta said the new units would also produce biogas, green energy and manure."Waste should not remain waste; Delhi should use it as wealth," she said, adding that new technologies were being introduced for waste segregation and processing.She said waste and cattle dung would be used to produce biogas and manure as part of efforts to build a technology-driven waste management system.Gupta said the government was taking up several measures to address pollution, including work on landfill waste, cleaning the Yamuna, dust mitigation, plantation, road infrastructure and waste management."Our government is tackling pollution from a 360-degree perspective to ensure it gradually decreases. We are working on every aspect, be it addressing the mountains of garbage, cleaning the Yamuna, improving road infrastructure, or managing waste, to ensure the people of Delhi enjoy better air quality. Our resolve and policies are absolutely clear, and we are working 24x7 in the public interest," she said.The chief minister also reviewed the progress of waste disposal work with officials and directed them to accelerate the work according to the stipulated timeline.She said the garbage mountains at Bhalswa, Ghazipur and Okhla had caused inconvenience to people travelling through these areas and said the government was continuing efforts to eliminate them.
Article Summary: Gupta said the Delhi government had reclaimed 100 acres of land across the city's three landfill sites over the past one-and-a-half years. She said almost all legacy waste at Okhla that existed before January 2025 had been processed. Gupta said the new units would also produce biogas, green energy and manure.

Article Title: India-US trade talks hit ‘plateau’: Sitharaman says further give-and-take ‘very, very difficult’
Article Text:
Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman

India stresses strategic autonomy in trade negotiations

India-EU pact opens market access

India and US have reached a “plateau” in negotiations over their bilateral trade agreement, with further concessions from either side likely to be "very very difficult", finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman said on Monday. Speaking at the Munich Leaders Meeting in New Delhi, she said that while negotiations are still underway, any progress from here would depend on whether there was limited room for compromise on either side.“The agreement negotiations are still ongoing, although we'd like to believe that both the sides have reached a plateau beyond which giving or taking might be very, very difficult. But maybe if there are rooms to operate from, both sides would do it,” Sitharaman said.She said the agreement was still being “hard and very rigorously negotiated” and that India has a trade surplus with the US. “But what is the predominant feature of the trade relations between India and the US? The trade balance is very much in our favor.”Sitharaman said that the US would naturally want to reduce this trade imbalance and address what it sees as losses built up over the years.She also said that the way countries negotiate trade deals was changing, with governments now looking beyond traditional negotiations to address trade imbalances.“Negotiation used to be the only platform through which countries could highlight the discrepancies, highlight the lop-sidedness and say, would we want to correct this?” she said.“Tariff was an instrument of negotiation, and tariff had a certain framework within which you will apply it. Today framework is there, tariffs are going,” she said, while stressing that countries still need to negotiate and find “some give and take”.Sitharaman was also asked about maintaining strategic autonomy while negotiating bilateral trade agreements with European countries, including in the context of India procuring Russian oil."There is no Lindsay Graham Bill in Europe...," she said.On the broader question of how bilateral trade agreements can protect a country's interests in an era of multilateralism, Sitharaman said countries were increasingly choosing bilateral partnerships where they saw greater benefit.“Countries choose where multilateralism would benefit them, and there are some unique bilaterals which countries choose to have. The balance is somewhat tilted in favour of the bilateral rather than the multilateral,” she said.She said countries were now increasingly looking for new trade partners and strengthening those relationships through agreements.“Countries are now rapidly catching up with — I would put the EU-India also in a bilateral mode -because it's one in the name of union, but of course within them they have. So, bilaterals today are catching up far more than even initiating or beginning a multilateral. It's not deliberate, but in a way, if you don't do it, you're not moving forward. Countries will have to choose new partners for their trade and strengthen the tie through an agreement. And therefore, newer partnerships are being searched for, and they are tied up bilaterally.”FM Sitharaman cited the India-EU trade agreement as a major example of India's approach to negotiating trade pacts while protecting domestic interests.She said India had opened 92.5 per cent of its tariff lines and around 97 per cent of tariff value under the agreement. The EU, meanwhile, had opened 99 per cent in value terms and possibly 97 per cent of tariff lines.According to Sitharaman, greater access to the European market could support employment in labour-intensive sectors, including footwear, textiles, toys and processed products. Many of these sectors are linked to micro and small enterprises.“Those are all in the micro and small medium industry segment, which are labor-intensive,” Sitharaman said, adding that greater access to the European market could generate “more exports, more jobs”.Sitharaman said bilateral trade agreements were becoming increasingly important as multilateral institutions have weakened.“Multilateralism is not going to go away. But multilateralism has weakened,” she said.She also stressed that multilateralism should continue even as countries increasingly pursue bilateral agreements.“Multilateralism is not going to go away and multilateralism shouldn't go away,” Sitharaman said.The Munich Leaders Meeting, being held in the National Capital, provides a platform for about 100 senior decision-makers and experts to discuss opportunities for stronger cooperation among emerging and middle powers amid profound geopolitical change. Discussions include geoeconomic developments, trade and connectivity, maritime security, defence cooperation and other key international challenges.
Article Summary: Finance minister Nirmala Sitharaman says India and US have reached a 'plateau' in negotiations over their bilateral trade agreement. She said any progress from here would depend on whether there was limited room for compromise on either side. She also said the way countries negotiate trade deals was changing, with governments now looking beyond traditional negotiations to address trade imbalances.

Article Title: Jio IPO sees bumper demand: India's largest public issue fully subscribed in just 100 minutes of opening
Article Text:
The IPO is open to retail investors, employees and eligible Reliance shareholders.

Jio IPO

Jio IPO: Jio Platforms' $3.2 billion initial public offering (IPO) was fully subscribed within less than two hours of bidding opening on Wednesday, as investors rushed to participate in India's biggest-ever share sale. The offering is also the first IPO from billionaire Mukesh Ambani 's Reliance group in two decades.According to a PTI report, the Jio IPO was fully subscribed within 100 minutes of its opening on October 21.The rapid subscription was notable because large IPOs in India often see a slow start, with institutional investors typically placing their bids closer to the closing deadline. By comparison, the National Stock Exchange of India's share sale recently attracted subscriptions for just 42% of the shares on offer on its first day. Hyundai Motor India's IPO had received bids for only 18% of its offering on the opening day.Also Read | Jio IPO, India’s largest public issue, opens for subscription: Price band, GMP to brokerage views - top 10 things to know The IPO is open to retail investors, employees and eligible Reliance shareholders. The issue will close on Friday, with shares priced in a band of Rs 1,065 to Rs 1,119 apiece.Exchange data showed that institutional investors had bid for 3.25 times the shares reserved for them by Wednesday. Retail participation was lower at that stage, with individual investors applying for 0.22 times their reserved quota.Retail investors have been allocated around one-third of the total offering.The IPO values Jio Platforms at as much as $108.3 billion. Once trading begins on October 28, the company could rank among India's largest listed companies by market capitalisation.Earlier this week, Jio Platforms allotted shares worth $853 million to domestic and international investors, including the Abu Dhabi Investment Authority and BlackRock. The anchor investor portion attracted bids exceeding $25 billion, according to a Reuters report.Backed by global investors such as Meta, Google's parent company Alphabet and other institutional investors, Jio Platforms houses India's largest telecom operator. With more than 500 million subscribers, the business is the world's second-largest telecom operator within a single country, behind China Mobile.This is Reliance's first IPO since 2006. Jio Platforms' telecom business, led by Ambani's son Akash, began operations in 2016. Its strategy was built around the expectation that Indians would use the internet much more extensively if access became almost free. By offering inexpensive data and free voice calls, Jio quickly gained market share from competitors such as Bharti Airtel and Vodafone Idea.
Article Summary: Jio IPO was fully subscribed within 100 minutes of its opening on October 21. The rapid subscription was notable because large IPOs in India often see a slow start. The IPO is open to retail investors, employees and eligible Reliance shareholders. The issue will close on Friday, with shares priced in a band of Rs 1,065 to Rs1,119 apiece.

Article Title: LPG consumption down, diesel & petrol sales up in September
Article Text:
LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier

NEW DELHI: LPG demand fell by over 9% year-on-year in Sept, while petrol and diesel sales registered growth of 7% and 5%, respectively, provisional data released by the Petroleum Planning and Analysis Cell (PPAC) showed.LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier.Month-on-month consumption, however, registered a growth of 8%, up from 2.4 MT.Petrol sales increased from 3.4 MT in Sept last year to 3.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose from 6.8 MT to 7.1 MT. Petrol and diesel consumption had registered year-on-year growth of 7.9% and 6.5%, respectively, in July.While petrol is largely used as an automobile fuel and its consumption is commensurate with the increasing number of vehicles, diesel is consumed by transport vehicles for passenger and freight movement, besides being used in the agricultural sector.Erratic monsoon conditions due to El Nino boosted demand for diesel for irrigation.Cumulative petrol consumption during Apr-Sept in the current financial year increased 7% to 22.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose 4.8% to 47.9 MT. In contrast, LPG consumption declined 14.9% to 13.8 MT from 16.2 MT during the corresponding period of 2025-26.
Article Summary: LPG consumption in Sept was recorded at 2.6 million tonnes (MT), compared to 2.9 MT during the same month a year earlier. Petrol sales increased from 3.4 MT in Sept last year to 3.6 MT, while diesel consumption rose from 6.8 MT to 7.1 MT.

Article Title: Google parent Alphabet loses $500 billion in market value as AI spending spooks investors
Article Text:
The $500 billion wipeout marked the second-largest single-day loss in market value recorded by a company, after chipmaker Nvidia lost nearly $600 billion in early 2025

AI spending raises questions about returns

Why investors are becoming cautious about AI

Shares of Google parent Alphabet plunged more than 12% on Thursday, wiping out around $500 billion in market value in one of the biggest single-day losses in stock market history. The sell-off reflected growing investor concerns over the company's escalating artificial intelligence spending, slowing growth in its search advertising business and uncertainty over how quickly its investments will generate returns.The decline marked Alphabet's worst single-day fall on record, exceeding its losses during the Covid-19 pandemic and the 2008 financial crisis, according to CNN. The market value erosion was the second-largest single-day loss recorded by a company, after chipmaker Nvidia lost nearly $600 billion in early 2025.The sharp fall followed Alphabet's quarterly earnings report, released on Wednesday, which showed sales below analysts' expectations. Investors were particularly concerned about the outlook for Google's search advertising business, which has long been a major source of revenue and profit.The company is facing growing competition from artificial intelligence-powered chatbots that allow users to seek information without relying on traditional search results. Investors fear this shift could weaken Google's advertising business if consumers increasingly turn to AI tools, including those developed by competitors, to find answers online.The concern is that the transition could happen faster than Google can adapt its business model. Jed Ellerbroek, portfolio manager at Argent Capital Management, told CNN that the displacement of traditional search could happen “faster than Google can react to it and pivot their business.”Alongside concerns about its core search business, Alphabet's rapidly rising expenditure on AI infrastructure has intensified scrutiny of its financial performance.The company reported $51.4 billion in capital expenditure in the third quarter alone, compared with $91.4 billion for the whole of 2025. The spending includes investments in data centres and computing infrastructure needed to develop and operate AI services.While technology companies are pouring hundreds of billions of dollars into infrastructure to compete in the AI race, investors are increasingly questioning whether the spending will translate into sustainable profits.A key concern for Alphabet is its free cash flow, which measures the cash remaining after operating expenses and capital investments. The company recorded negative free cash flow for a second consecutive quarter, according to CNN. Before this year, Google had not reported a negative figure for any quarter since going public in 2004.Negative free cash flow does not necessarily indicate that a company is unprofitable. However, it means less cash is available after investment spending to fund shareholder returns, including dividends and share buybacks, or to support other business priorities.Alphabet's performance stood in contrast to Microsoft, which reported $18.6 billion in free cash flow for the third quarter despite continuing to invest heavily in AI infrastructure. Microsoft's shares ended Thursday's session largely unchanged, while Alphabet suffered a double-digit decline.“We are now getting to see who is spending rationally on AI and who is not,” Richard Reyle, chief investment officer at Questar Capital Partners, told CNN.The sell-off highlights a broader shift in how markets are evaluating the AI boom. Investors are no longer looking only at the scale of companies' investments or the growth potential of the technology. They are also assessing whether those investments can generate adequate returns, how much cash they consume and whether AI could undermine existing revenue streams.Alphabet is attempting to expand its AI capabilities while defending its dominant search business. Its investments could help it compete in a rapidly changing technology market, but the returns remain uncertain as the industry races to build data centres and secure computing capacity.Even the prospect of future demand from AI companies does not guarantee immediate profitability. Although AI firms are committing to large amounts of computing power, the financial benefits depend on whether demand continues to grow and whether the infrastructure can be monetised at a sufficient scale.Technology companies are also increasingly turning to debt and financial markets to fund their ambitions, raising questions about the sustainability of the industry's capital spending.“Everybody is trying to get through the door at the same time, and it gives people pause,” Ted Mortonson, a technology-focused investment strategist at Baird, told CNN.For Alphabet, the challenge is to demonstrate that its massive AI investments can produce profitable growth without weakening the cash-generating search business that has supported the company for years. Thursday's steep decline suggests investors are demanding clearer evidence of those returns rather than accepting spending growth as a sign of future success.
Article Summary: Shares of Google parent Alphabet plunged more than 12% on Thursday, wiping out around $500 billion in market value. The sell-off reflected growing investor concerns over the company's escalating artificial intelligence spending, slowing growth in its search advertising business and uncertainty over how quickly its investments will generate returns. The decline marked Alphabet's worst single- day fall on record.

Article Title: Trump moves to end H-1B visa deference: What it means for Indians stuck in the Green Card backlog
Article Text:
Trump’s H-1B deference move.

“Removing deference would not itself change green card queue positions or automatically invalidate existing H-1B approvals. However, it could affect how subsequent petitions are assessed while individuals wait for permanent residency.”

“For Indian H-1B holders in the EB-2/EB-3 backlog, this rule changes the nature of the green-card wait itself. Most are living on three-year AC21 extensions, four, five, six renewals over a decade. Today each renewal presumes the last approval was correct. Under the proposed rule, every renewal becomes a fresh trial of eligibility, with specialty occupation, wage level, and employer relationship all back on the table,” he said.

Indians accounted for 71% of H-1B visa recipients.

What is the US deference policy, and what could change?

How the proposed change could affect H-1B extensions.

How could this affect Indian H-1B professionals waiting for green cards?

More scrutiny, additional paperwork for employers?

Why does the Trump administration want to end deference?

Timeline of changes to the US deference policy.

What happens next?

For Indian professionals working in the US, an H-1B extension is more than a routine immigration formality. It is a crucial bridge to maintaining legal status and keeping their path to permanent residency, or a green card, alive as they navigate a backlog that can stretch for decades.Many rely on successive extensions while waiting for their employment-based green cards. A proposed change by the Trump administration could make that process more uncertain, even for workers whose previous visa petitions were approved.The administration has proposed scrapping the US immigration policy known as “deference to prior approvals”. Under the policy, US Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) generally gives weight to an earlier favourable decision when reviewing an extension petition involving the same employer, worker and underlying facts, unless certain exceptions apply.The policy requires immigration officers to consider previous approvals, while the proposed change could make it easier for them to reassess a worker’s eligibility.The proposal, published on October 14, is not yet a final rule. If implemented, it could mean closer scrutiny of extension applications from Indian H-1B holders, including those who have spent years building their lives and careers in the US while waiting for employment-based green cards.The change could also affect workers in other visa categories, including L-1 intracompany transfers.Rajiv Dabhadkar, founder of the National Organisation for Software and Technology Professionals (NOSTOPS), told TOI,Immigration attorney Bhumireddy Sai Srinivas Reddy told TOI the proposal could make the long wait for permanent residency more uncertain for Indian H-1B holders.Indians accounted for about 70 per cent of all H-1B beneficiaries in fiscal year 2025, according to USCIS data, making them a significant group potentially affected by any change to how work visa extensions are adjudicated.The US Department of Homeland Security (DHS) and USCIS have proposed removing a provision under 8 CFR 214.1(c)(5), which generally requires the agency to give “deference to a prior approval” when adjudicating a request to extend a non-immigrant worker's petition involving the same parties and underlying facts.The DHS explains: “When adjudicating a request filed on Form I-129 (Petition for a Nonimmigrant Worker) involving the same parties and the same underlying facts, USCIS gives deference to its prior determination of the petitioner's, applicant's, or beneficiary's eligibility.”However, deference is not an unconditional guarantee of approval.Under the existing regulation, USCIS can depart from an earlier determination if there was a material error, a material change or new material information that adversely affects eligibility.Employers use Form I-129 to petition for foreign workers in several temporary employment categories, including H-1B, L-1, O-1 and other non-immigrant classifications.If the proposal is finalised, USCIS officers would still be able to consider previous approvals where relevant. However, they would no longer be required to begin from a position of deference to an earlier decision.The proposed change would therefore alter the framework for reviewing extension petitions, rather than automatically changing the basic eligibility requirements for each visa category.The proposed change could be particularly consequential for Indian professionals who have spent years working in the US while waiting for employment-based green cards.The H-1B visa allows US employers to hire foreign workers in specialised occupations, with an annual cap of 65,000 visas and another 20,000 for qualifying US advanced-degree graduates.It is generally granted for up to three years and can be extended for another three, with certain workers eligible for extensions beyond the usual six-year limit while pursuing employment-based green cards.For many Indian professionals, the green-card process can stretch over decades because of the high demand for employment-based immigrant visas and country-specific limits on their allocation.A recent analysis by the National Foundation for American Policy (NFAP) estimated that nearly one million Indians are stuck in the US employment-based green-card backlog, accounting for close to 79 per cent of the estimated 1.26 million people waiting in the first three employment-based preference categories.The NFAP analysis also estimated that an Indian professional entering the queue in 2026 could face a potential wait of 179 years in the EB-2 category and 38 years in EB-3, under its modelling assumptions.These projections show the scale of the backlog, although actual waiting periods depend on factors such as visa availability, category and priority date, as well as future policy changes.This would not automatically mean denials, but could increase documentation requirements and uncertainty over processing times.Dabhadkar said, “Additional scrutiny could mean more evidence requests, higher legal and administrative costs, and uncertainty over continued employment, affecting workers’ career decisions and long-term planning.”If USCIS officers seek additional evidence, employers may have to submit more detailed documentation relating to job duties, compensation, work locations, business operations, contracts and workers' qualifications.Employers may also need to demonstrate that workers continue to meet the eligibility requirements of their respective visa categories, rather than relying heavily on the fact that an earlier petition was approved.An analysis by the Vasquez Law Firm said the proposal could change how USCIS reviews subsequent petitions.“A worker may feel the practical effects even though the employer is often the petitioner,” the firm noted, explaining that employers may have to document the offered role, business operations, compensation, contracts, work location and the worker's qualifications again.The firm also said workers may need records showing that they have continued to maintain their non-immigrant status.DHS estimates that the proposed rule would impose nearly $133,987 in additional annual costs on petitioners and lead to around 6,044 additional requests for evidence (RFEs) each year.The department says the change could increase adjudication workloads and operational costs as officers spend more time reassessing eligibility and reviewing additional evidence.Reddy said delays caused by additional evidence requests could have consequences for workers whose employment authorisation depends on timely decisions.“The real risk is delay, not denial. More RFEs mean more petitions pending past the 240-day work-authorization window and a worker who hits day 241 must stop working, even with an approved I-140 and a decade of lawful status. With automatic EAD extensions gone, an H-4 spouse's work authorization can lapse in the same queue,” he said.For employers, the consequences could include greater legal and administrative expenses, more time spent preparing extension petitions and less certainty in workforce planning. For workers, additional requests for evidence could prolong the decision-making process.The Trump administration argues that the existing policy could limit the ability of immigration officers to examine applications independently.In its proposal, the DHS said the deference policy may have resulted in “perpetuating erroneous prior approvals and creating an environment in which fraudulent and meritless petitions are less likely to be detected before approval”.The department also argued that some employers may have interpreted the policy as reducing their obligation to show that a worker continues to meet the requirements of the requested visa classification.According to the proposal, the existing regulation effectively shifts the burden from the petitioner to the USCIS officer, who must justify departing from an earlier approval.The DHS says removing the requirement would better align its regulations and adjudication practices with its interpretation of the Immigration and Nationality Act, under which the burden of establishing eligibility for immigration benefits rests with the petitioner.“Removing the deference requirement would also help to ensure that USCIS officers fully review the facts and evidence in every case to ensure continued eligibility,” the proposal states.The policy has changed several times over the years. USCIS first issued guidance on deference in 2004, rescinded it in 2017, and reinstated it in its Policy Manual in 2021. The DHS formally codified the policy in December 2024. The latest proposal would reverse that codification.The proposal is open for public comments until November 13, 2026. Interested parties can submit feedback through the federal rulemaking portal, citing DHS Docket No. USCIS-2026-0529.Employers, immigration attorneys, and other stakeholders can use the consultation period to raise concerns about the potential impact on workers and businesses.For Indian professionals, the proposal would change how extension petitions are reviewed, not H-1B eligibility requirements or the existing six-year limit. Current rules remain in effect until a final rule is published and takes effect.
Article Summary: The administration has proposed scrapping the US immigration policy known as ‘deference to prior approvals’ Under the policy, US Citizenship and Immigration Services (USCIS) generally gives weight to an earlier favourable decision. If implemented, it could mean closer scrutiny of extension applications from Indian H-1B holders.

Article Title: Prince William inherited the $1.3 billion Duchy of Cornwall, spanning 128,000 acres, after Queen Elizabeth II’s death; earning $31 million annually from it, he now plans to sell 20% to fund housing an
Article Text:
Prince William plans to sell 20% of the Duchy of Cornwall estate to support housing and green projects. (Photo: Getty)

Why Prince William wants to reshape the Duchy of Cornwall

Tackling homelessness through housing projects

The 128,000-acre Duchy of Cornwall is valued at $1.3 billion and provides Prince William with nearly $31 million in annual income. (Photo: Getty)

Why William is redirecting money from Dartmoor Prison

Princess Kate's early childhood initiative finds a partner in the Duchy

Cornwall remains important to William and his family

Prince William is using one of the British royal family's most valuable assets to pursue causes close to his heart, with plans to sell a portion of his vast estate to fund housing, environmental recovery and renewable energy projects.The Prince of Wales , 44, took control of the Duchy of Cornwall after the death of his grandmother, Queen Elizabeth II, in September 2022. The estate, which spans more than 128,000 acres, is valued at over $1.3 billion and provides William with an annual private income of nearly $31 million.However, the future king is looking beyond the traditional role of the estate as a source of income. According to a report by The Times, William plans to sell around 20% of the Duchy's assets, potentially raising an estimated $670 million to support a new approach centred on social needs, nature recovery and clean energy.Established in 1337, the Duchy of Cornwall was created to provide an income for the heir to the British throne and support the household and public responsibilities associated with the role. It has traditionally consisted of land, property and other assets managed on behalf of the heir apparent.William inherited control of the estate when his father, King Charles III, became monarch following Queen Elizabeth II's death.When William eventually becomes king, control will pass to his eldest son, Prince George, continuing the centuries-old tradition.Under William's leadership, however, the estate is being encouraged to take a more active role in addressing local challenges. The reported plan to sell a fifth of its assets would allow it to focus its resources on five key areas, including Cornwall, Dartmoor, the Isles of Scilly, Bath and parts of London.Duchy chief executive Will Bax has outlined a vision in which the organisation evaluates its presence according to the positive impact it can deliver."If we don’t see an opportunity for positive impact, then perhaps we don’t need to be a part of that place," Bax told The Times."But where there is social need and where there is environmental challenge and where there is an opportunity to enable change, then we’ll be a great partner in working with people to achieve that."The approach reflects William's broader interest in using his position and resources to address social and environmental concerns.One of William's priorities for the Duchy is addressing homelessness, an issue he has also made central to his wider Homewards initiative.The project seeks to develop practical, locally driven solutions to homelessness, bringing together organisations and communities to explore ways of preventing people from losing their homes.In 2024, Ben Murphy, estate director at the Duchy of Cornwall, explained that William had asked the estate to address homelessness in Cornwall and other areas where it operates."As one of his key priorities for the Duchy of Cornwall, Prince William asked us to address the homelessness challenge within Cornwall and other areas where the estate resides," Murphy said.The Duchy is already developing social housing in Nansledan, near Newquay in Cornwall. The project is part of a broader effort to create communities that combine housing with local services and commercial spaces.Another planned development on Market Street in Newquay aims to create a new high street featuring independent businesses, local artisans and community enterprises. The project is expected to be completed in 2028 and is intended to help strengthen the local economy.These developments illustrate how the estate's property portfolio could be used to support communities beyond its traditional financial role.The Prince of Wales has also taken steps to redirect income from an estate asset that is no longer being used for its original purpose.Dartmoor Prison has been vacant since July 2024 and had previously brought William around $2 million a year in rent. Instead of keeping the rental income, he decided to use the same annual amount to support the local community through the Princetown Community Fund.According to a September press release, the fund will support projects delivering lasting social, economic and environmental benefits for people in Princetown and the surrounding Dartmoor area.The decision aligns with the wider direction of the Duchy under William: ensuring that assets and income are connected to the needs of the communities in which the estate operates.William's plans also intersect with the work of his wife, Princess Kate, particularly her focus on early childhood development and the role of nature in children's well-being.Kate's Centre for Early Childhood has partnered with the Duchy of Cornwall to explore how time spent outdoors can support the mental well-being and development of young children, as well as the people who care for them.The collaboration, launched in Nansledan, examines how nature, creativity and relationships can help children develop the social and emotional skills that contribute to lifelong health and well-being."This project is about exploring how nature, creativity and relationships can best support the healthy development of babies and young children," Kate said in a video."We believe that taking a whole-child approach is important, and nature becomes a wonderful place to explore how we can successfully nurture the social and emotional skills that underpin lifelong health and wellbeing."The initiative connects the Duchy's environmental ambitions with Kate's long-standing interest in the early years of childhood, highlighting how the estate's land can be used for projects that benefit families and local communities.Beyond its financial significance and public initiatives, the Duchy of Cornwall also holds a place in Prince William and Kate’s family life.Cornwall and the Isles of Scilly are among the destinations where the family spends time together. The Prince and Princess of Wales have also shared photographs and videos of their children, Prince George, Princess Charlotte and Prince Louis, taken in Cornwall as part of their birthday celebrations this year.
Article Summary: Prince William plans to sell 20% of the Duchy of Cornwall estate to support housing and green projects. The 128,000-acre estate is valued at over $1.3 billion and provides William with an annual private income of nearly $31 million. The Prince of Wales is looking beyond the traditional role of the estate as a source of income.

Article Title: Family gets no proper food, 11-month-old baby not given milk on 15-hour Delhi-Melbourne Singapore Airlines flight in 2020; 6 years later, airline ordered to pay Rs 50,000 plus litigation expenses

NEW DELHI: A passenger's complaint that his family, including an 11-month-old baby, was not served adequate food on a 15-hour flight has led the Punjab State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission to hold Singapore Airlines liable for deficiency in service, according to a report by Bar and Bench.The commission ruled that an airline cannot escape responsibility for providing regular meals simply because passengers have not asked for special food.It also pointed out that Singapore Airlines had failed to establish that the family was served adequate food during the journey.The dispute dates back to March 4, 2020, when Jaspreet Singh 's wife, mother-in-law and infant daughter flew from Delhi to Melbourne.Singh alleged that the family was not provided proper meals during the journey and that even milk for his 11-month-old daughter was not made available.After Singh raised the issue through an email, the airline initially promised to look into the complaint. However, its subsequent response was that the passengers had not placed a request for vegetarian or special meals. It also asked Singh to take up the matter with his travel agent.Unhappy with the response, Singh approached the district consumer commission in Ropar. He sought a refund of Rs 1.25 lakh towards the tickets and ₹10 lakh in compensation.In January 2023, the district commission ordered Singapore Airlines and the travel agent to refund the ticket fare with 7% annual interest. It also awarded Rs 25,000 as compensation and Rs 11,000 towards litigation expenses.The airline challenged the decision before the state commission, maintaining that no special meal request had been made and that food from its regular menu had been served.The state commission rejected this argument, holding that passengers need not request special meals to be entitled to ordinary food on a long-duration flight. It further observed that the airline had not furnished sufficient evidence to show that the family had received adequate meals.However, the commission took into account that the passengers had completed their journey and said a full ticket refund would be disproportionate.In an order dated October 7, it reduced the relief and directed Singapore Airlines to pay Rs 50,000 as consolidated compensation for mental agony and harassment, besides litigation expenses.The amount is to be paid to Singh within 45 days, Bar and Bench reported.
Article Summary: A passenger's complaint that his family, including an 11-month-old baby, was not served adequate food on a 15-hour flight has led the Punjab State Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission to hold Singapore Airlines liable for deficiency in service. The dispute dates back to March 4, 2020, when Jaspreet Singh's wife, mother-in-law and infant daughter flew from Delhi to Melbourne.

BENGALURU: Nearly six years after a Bengaluru woman’s fixed deposit matured, a consumer commission has ordered a credit co-operative society to return her Rs 3 lakh investment with interest, holding it liable for failing to honour its repayment obligation.The Bengaluru Urban District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission has also directed the society to pay Rs 35,000 towards compensation and litigation expenses to the 66-year-old depositor, Sabitha.The dispute dates back to October 2020, when Sabitha’s three-year fixed deposit with the society became due for repayment. She had invested Rs 3 lakh on October 11, 2017, at an annual interest rate of 9.5%.When Sabitha approached the society after the deposit matured, she was asked to return a month later. A second visit in November 2020 also failed to secure her money, with the society citing the time required to process the repayment.The woman continued visiting the society and seeking the release of her principal and accumulated interest, but the payment never came.She told the commission that she needed the money for personal and family commitments and that being denied access to her savings had caused financial hardship.After years of waiting, she sent the society a legal notice on February 25, 2026, seeking repayment. The society neither responded to the notice nor returned the deposit, following which she filed a complaint under the Consumer Protection Act, 2019, alleging deficiency in service and unfair trade practice.The III Additional Bengaluru Urban District Consumer Disputes Redressal Commission examined the fixed deposit receipt, Sabitha's affidavit and other documents submitted in support of her complaint.The society did not appear before the commission despite being served notice. It also placed no evidence on record to dispute the woman's claims.The commission found that the society had failed to repay the deposit even after its maturity and that the prolonged withholding of the money had caused the complainant financial difficulties and mental distress.In its September 28, 2026, order, the commission, headed by president Shivarama K and comprising members Rekha Sayannavar and Suma Anilkumar, directed the society to return the Rs 3 lakh deposit with 9.5% annual interest calculated from October 11, 2017, until the amount is realised.It additionally awarded Sabitha Rs 25,000 for mental agony and hardship and Rs 10,000 towards litigation expenses.The society has been given 45 days to comply. If it misses the deadline, the Rs 35,000 awarded as compensation and litigation costs will carry 9% annual interest from the date of the order until payment.
Article Summary: Bengaluru woman's fixed deposit matured nearly six years ago. Credit co- operative society failed to honour its repayment obligation. Woman, 66, awarded Rs 35,000 towards compensation and litigation expenses. Society given 45 days to comply with the order.

Article Title: India ready to share its battle-tested expertise with Asean partners to boost joint capabilities: Rajnath
Article Text:
Defence minister Rajnath Singh addressing the 13th ASEAN Defence Ministers’ Meeting (ADMM)

Rajnath Singh with Australian and Japanese defence ministers

NEW DELHI: India’s extensive expertise in counter-terrorism is not theoretical classroom knowledge but it is an experience hard-earned on the ground through decades of directly confronting complex, cross-border security challenges, defence minister Rajnath Singh said in the Philippines on Thursday.Addressing the 13th ASEAN Defence Ministers’ Meeting (ADMM) - Plus in Cebu, Rajnath underlined that “every strategy of India has been tested, refined and proven in the crucible of real-world operations” and that India stands fully prepared to share its practical, battle-tested experience with ADMM-Plus partners through joint exercises, capacity-building programmes, and robust intelligence sharing to strengthen collective capabilities. He reaffirmed the country’s commitment to collective regional security and eradication of terrorism in all its forms.Rajnath said this proactive, battle-tested doctrine was decisively demonstrated during Operation Sindoor, when India dismantled terrorist infrastructure and enforced a non-negotiable red line against state-sponsored terror. He stressed that counter-terrorism remains an important area of cooperation under the ADMM-Plus framework, and India and Malaysia are co-chairing the experts’ working group on counter-terrorism for the 2024 to 2027 cycle.Rajnath highlighted that by deploying frontline warships, India has successfully escorted thousands of merchant vessels and thwarted dozens of high-seas hijackings, extending protection to commercial shipping irrespective of flag or nationality. He termed the security of commercial shipping as India’s responsibility. “In an era where global trade routes face complex transnational threats, India stands ready to move beyond rhetoric. There is a need for effective action, regular operational presence and international cooperation. India will continue serving as a reliable net security provider in the Indian Ocean Region and the wider Indo-Pacific,” he said.The minister highlighted the importance of youth engagement in strengthening India-ASEAN defence cooperation, stating that the shared demographic profile and aspirations of the young populations provide a strong foundation for deeper regional partnership. He proposed the establishment of a dedicated defence ‘Youth Bridge’ to enhance institutional people-to-people connectivity, promote digital innovation and facilitate capacity building in line with ADMM-Plus initiatives.On the sidelines of ADMM-Plus, Rajnath met Japanese minister of defence Shinjiro Koizumi, and Australian minister for defence Richard Marles and posted a picture with them. “JAI: Japan, Australia, India”, the defence Minister posted on X, with him holding hands of both Marles and Koizumi, as he stood in the middle.At the forum, the minister reiterated that India attaches importance to ASEAN centrality and a secure, open, inclusive, resilient and rule-based Indo-Pacific, where peace and stability are not just aspirations but a result of collective commitment. He stated that its strategic engagement with ASEAN is long-term and rooted in shared interests, mutual respect and practical cooperation. He recalled that the second ASEAN-India defence ministers’ informal meeting in Kuala Lumpur in Oct last year reaffirmed the commitment to advancing the defence and security components of the ASEAN-India Comprehensive Strategic Partnership and the ASEAN-India Plan of Action for 2026 to 2030.On the theme of 13th ADMM-Plus ‘Navigating Our Future, Together’, Rajnath stated it resonates with India’s foreign and defence policy paradigms as well as its civilisational ethos of ‘Sarve Bhavantu Sukhinah’ (May all beings be happy) that reflects the aspiration for the happiness, prosperity, and well-being of all the people across the world. “This theme reminds us that our greatest strength lies in our solidarity and the shared ability to leverage our geographic, economic and strategic diversity. India believes in an international system built on mutual trust, co-operation, and collective responsibility. It is this precise collaborative spirit that empowers us to overcome the challenges to peace and order,” he said.The minister described maritime cooperation as crucial to India’s engagement with ASEAN during 2026, highlighting New Delhi’s designation of 2026 as the ASEAN-India Year of Maritime Cooperation and the conduct of the second ASEAN-India Maritime Exercise. He emphasised that India does not merely preach the tenets of international maritime law; it is a steadfast practitioner of global laws concerning maritime security. “Our commitment to ensuring the freedom of navigation and safeguarding global Sea Lines of Communication is backed by a continuous, decades-long operational legacy. Since 2008, the Indian Navy has maintained an uninterrupted, active presence in highly volatile corridors like the Gulf of Aden, without coercion or unilateral actions that undermine the rights of other nations,” he said.Rajnath said India’s emphasis on the rule of law, particularly the United Nations Convention on the Law of the Sea, and its advocacy for freedom of navigation and overflight are not directed against any country but are meant to safeguard the collective interests of all regional stakeholders who depend on open sea lanes and stable maritime governance.
Article Summary: Rajnath Singh underlined that “every strategy of India has been tested, refined and proven in the crucible of real-world operations’ He reaffirmed the country’s commitment to collective regional security and eradication of terrorism in all its forms.
